Get district-level police crime statistics

Source: R/pks_get.R
pks_get.Rd

Downloads the district (Kreis) tables of the German Police Crime Statistics (PKS) from a versioned data release, as published by the Bundeskriminalamt or harmonized to one territorial boundary and offence classification. Files are cached and checked against the SHA-256 checksums of the release manifest.

Usage

pks_get(
  years = NULL,
  offence = NULL,
  harmonize_to = "latest",
  weights = c("population", "area"),
  version = "latest",
  source = c("release", "bka"),
  cache = TRUE,
  lang = NULL
)

Arguments

years

Integer vector of reporting years, or NULL (default) for all years of the release.

offence

Offences to return, or NULL (default) for all. Each element can be an offence key ("435*00"), a short name in English or German ("residential_burglary", "wohnungseinbruch"), a full label ("Wohnungseinbruchdiebstahl") or a part of a label ("einbruch", which selects both burglary keys). An exact key, name or label wins over a part. Capitals, spaces and umlauts do not matter. See pks_offences() for all keys and names. For the data as published, the published keys that feed the selected keys are returned.

harmonize_to

Target boundary year (Gebietsstand). "latest" (default) is the boundary of the release, read as released; another year harmonizes the data as published with the crosswalk of the release (forward only, so years must not be later than the target); NULL returns the data as published.

weights

Weights for districts that were split: "population" (default) or "area". Ignored for harmonize_to = NULL.

version

Data version such as "2026.1", or "latest" (default).

source

"release" (default) reads a data release. "bka", which will rebuild the spreadsheet years from the original BKA files, is not available yet.

cache

Keep downloaded files in the cache (default TRUE). With FALSE, files go to a temporary directory and are removed with the R session.

lang

Language of the offence labels in column offence_label and of the messages: "de" or "en". NULL (default) uses options(pksR.lang), otherwise the language of the R session. Harmonized data get the label of the harmonized key; data as published keep the published German label, or get the English label of the matching harmonized key.

Value

A tibble with one row per year, district (ags) and offence key. Columns are described in vignette("pksR"). Attributes: data_version, retrieved_at, boundary_year, weights and source_urls.

Deutsch

Lädt die Kreistabellen der Polizeilichen Kriminalstatistik (PKS) aus einer versionierten Datenveröffentlichung, wie vom Bundeskriminalamt veröffentlicht oder auf einen Gebietsstand und eine Straftatenzuordnung harmonisiert. Jede Datei wird gegen die SHA-256-Prüfsumme des Manifests geprüft und im Cache abgelegt.

  • years: Berichtsjahre, NULL für alle.

  • offence: Straftaten als Schlüssel ("435*00"), Kurzname auf Deutsch oder Englisch ("wohnungseinbruch", "residential_burglary"), vollständige Bezeichnung oder Teil einer Bezeichnung ("einbruch"). Groß- und Kleinschreibung, Leerzeichen und Umlaute spielen keine Rolle; eine genaue Übereinstimmung hat Vorrang. Übersicht: pks_offences().

  • harmonize_to: "latest" (Gebietsstand der Veröffentlichung), ein Jahr (Harmonisierung nur vorwärts) oder NULL (wie veröffentlicht).

  • weights: Gewichtung geteilter Kreise, "population" oder "area".

  • version: Datenversion, etwa "2026.1", oder "latest".

  • lang: Sprache der Bezeichnungen und Meldungen, "de" oder "en"; Voreinstellung options(pksR.lang), sonst die Sprache der R-Sitzung.

Ergebnis: ein Tibble mit einer Zeile je Jahr, Kreis und Straftatenschlüssel und den Attributen data_version, retrieved_at, boundary_year, weights und source_urls.

See also

Other data: pks_example()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# Total offences, harmonized to the latest boundary
total <- pks_get(offence = "total")

# Theft in total and both burglary keys, German labels
theft <- pks_get(offence = c("diebstahl", "einbruch"), lang = "de")

# As published by the BKA, two years
published <- pks_get(years = 2024:2025, harmonize_to = NULL)
}
